description: This case study is the NRC backgrounder on the Three Mile Island Unit 2 accident, the most serious accident in U.S. commercial nuclear power plant operating history, which partially melted down the reactor near Middletown, Pennsylvania, on 28 March 1979. The page gives a summary of events, an animated diagram of the sequence, health effects, the impact of the accident and a glossary and plant diagram. A failure in the secondary system stopped the main feedwater pumps, the turbine and reactor tripped, a pilot-operated relief valve stuck open while control room instruments indicated it closed, operators did not realise a loss-of-coolant accident was under way, and the lack of a core water level instrument led staff to assume the core was covered. Releases were very small with no detectable health effects, and the aftermath changed emergency response planning, operator training, human factors engineering, radiation protection and NRC oversight. Access: a web page with a printable version, free; no licence is stated. Caveats: a regulator's summary, not the commission report, with no plant data files. It suits cascading failure, human reliability and emergency planning scenario design, and relates to the NRC datasets on US nuclear facilities catalogued here.
